rule.description: Production code held dead by a compatibility switch that is permanently off: branches whose only guard is an inert package constant pinned to a falsy literal once and never written again, package-level symbols whose every reference site lies inside such dead code (or inside symbols already proven dead by the same fixpoint), and inert switches left unread. The switch, the dormant branch, and everything the branch holds alive exclusively form one retired compatibility layer that must be removed entirely.

checks.description: Detect branches whose only guard is a package constant pinned to a falsy literal exactly once at import time and never written again anywhere in the package.
checks.detected_relation: dormant branch -> inert compatibility switch (constant pinned off, no supported path can enable it)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The branch is unreachable in every supported configuration and is retained without a role, which is the core of dead code elimination for this case; the guard, not the body's content, makes the whole territory dead.

matches.evidence: Branch guarded by questionary.utils.LEGACY_EVENT_LOOP_COMPAT switches this async entry point to the retired prompt_toolkit 2 event-loop bootstrap; the constant is pinned to False exactly once and no code writes it again, so the branch can never run.
Branch guarded by questionary.prompts.common.LEGACY_LAYOUT_COMPAT returns a legacy 1.x two-window layout instead of building the supported single control window with search and validation messages.

Branch guarded by questionary.styles.LEGACY_STYLE_COMPAT routes this question's style through the retired 1.x merge helper; the switch is permanently off, so the supported style assembly always runs instead.

Branch guarded by questionary.prompts.USE_LEGACY_PROMPTS routes deprecated question names into the retired legacy registry instead of the supported one; the switch is never written truthy anywhere in the package.

Branch guarded by questionary.prompts.path.LEGACY_COMPLETION_COMPAT re-binds this completer's directory resolution to a legacy helper; the constant is inert, so the supported direct validation always applies.

checks.description: Detect package-level constants, functions, and registry data whose reference sites are all provably dead: either every use lies inside a dormant branch, or every use lies inside another symbol already proven unreachable by the same reference fixpoint.
checks.detected_relation: package-level symbol -> reference-site set (every site lies inside code that can never run)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: These symbols survive only through references from dead territory, so a repair that removes only the guard branches would leave exactly this set behind; complete elimination must follow the reference chain the dormant branches hold open.

matches.evidence: Duplicated 1.x selection-pointer constant; its only two readers are the retired list and rawlist factory imports, both inside dead code.
Registry mapping deprecated question names to the retired 1.x factories; its single read site is the dormant dispatch branch, so no supported path can reach any of its entries.
Legacy 1.x layout builder reproducing the two-window prompt_toolkit 2 layout without the search and validation rows; referenced only from the dormant branch in the supported layout builder.
Legacy 1.x directory-resolution wrapper that re-parents and silently skips nonexistent directories; its only reference site sits inside the dormant re-binding inside the completer constructor.
Retired factory reproducing pre-2.0 rawlist behaviour; referenced only as the legacy registry's value for the deprecated rawlist name.

Retired factory reproducing pre-2.0 list behaviour with the duplicated pointer constant consumed only here and by its rawlist sibling; referenced only as the legacy registry's value for the deprecated list name.
Retired factory reproducing pre-2.0 input behaviour; referenced only as the legacy registry's value for the deprecated input name.
Retired pre-2.0 style merge that concatenates merge lists without the current toolbar-workaround handling; referenced only from the dormant checkbox style branch.
prompt_toolkit 2 event-loop bootstrap delegating to the prompt_toolkit eventloop API; its only call site is the dormant branch in the async question entry point.

excluded: questionary.utils.ACTIVATED_ASYNC_MODE is live runtime state, not a dormant switch: it is written at runtime by activate_prompt_toolkit_async_mode() and read by the async asking path, so the rule's inert-constant test (exactly one write package-wide) never classifies it as inert.

The backwards-compatible question-name keys 'list', 'rawlist' and 'input' are live: the supported registry resolves them to the current factory functions at runtime. Only the retired duplicate routing behind the permanently-off switch is in scope.

Package boundary names -- dunders, module __all__ members, and names bound by imports in package __init__ modules -- are treated as externally reachable; the rule's zero-reference orphan branch never flags them.

Runtime-detected prompt_toolkit version handling (questionary.utils.is_prompt_toolkit_3() and the awaiting paths it selects between) is reachable under the prompt_toolkit >=2.0,<4.0 dependency range the project declares, so it is supported configuration handling, not dormant code.

The rule's third message, compat-inert-constant-unused, reports no matches on the injected tree by design: each retired switch is still read by its own dormant guard. It exists as the uniform-repair backstop -- after a repair that removes only the five guard branches, the retired switches become unread and are then reported -- so it contributes no injected matches of its own.
